about_details:
I consider myself a product of the American dream.
I realize I am privileged, because I am an American. Nothing more. Nothing less.
I worked all of my life starting at age 10 - shoveling snow, mowing lawns then a paper route... Did not have the opportunity for college, but still built a life that gave me a 40+ year marriage, two wonderful children, a home, many friends and successful career. Retired at 62. I am not rich but live comfortable and thankful for what we have. I enjoy: Cooking, Travel, Music, Stamp Collecting, Camping, Fishing, Gardening.
I worry about the hate and division in our country and it's future for my children and grandchildren... this is why I have started this FB page. This is also why I have become a very strong advocate for the Convention of States Action movement.
I am a firm believer in the vision our forefathers had when they wrote the Constitution and set the principles that founded our great Republic. This included the tools necessary to evolve and grow as our nation changed - Article V.
Feel free to send me a text and/or friend request for more information!

about_details:
"You make a living by what you get. You make a life by what you give." - Churchill
HOST of "Sinatra Standard Time" on KSDS-FM, Jazz88, San Diego
Author of "Sessions with Sinatra: Frank Sinatra & the Art of Recording," "Wouldn't It be Nice: Brian Wilson & the Making of 'Pet Sounds," and "Making Records: The Scenes Behind the Music" (with Phil Ramone)
Producer of "Frank Sinatra in Hollywood" (Warner/Reprise), "Frank Sinatra: A Voice in Time" (Columbia/Sony Music Legacy), and numerous other recording projects
Past producer and engineer of Nancy Sinatra's weekly "Nancy for Frank" show on Sirius-XM radio (Sirius 75 & XM 73)
Past member of the Board of Directors, NJ Hall of Fame; co-producer of the annual NJ Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony (NJPAC) featuring the participation of Nancy Sinatra, Bruce Springsteen, Jon Bon Jovi, Danny DeVito, Jack Nicholson, Susan Sarandon, Frankie Valli, Carl Lewis, Phoebe Snow, Toni Morrison, Buzz Aldrin, Yogi Berra, Steve Forbes, Mary Higgins Clark, and a host of other great New Jersey natives
National TV & radio appearances on Entertainment Tonight, CNN Sunday Morning, CBS Sunday Morning with Charles Osgood, CBS This Morning, Fresh Air (NPR), Morning Edition (NPR), Sid Marks' "Sounds of Sinatra," "The Joan Hamburg Show" (WOR) and various CNN, MSNBC, CNBC, PBS, NPR, and CBS radio & television programs.
Speaking engagements and lectures include George Washington University, Hofstra University, Museum of Television & Radio (NYC), and the Los Angeles Jazz Festival (2010).

When tyranny becomes law, rebellion becomes duty.
Know This, We Are Many They Are Few.
To Fear Death Is A Choice, And They Can't Hang Us All.
Courage is not the absence of fear but rather the judgment that something else is more important than fear
One day when they come for something you hold dear, you will regret, that you allowed them to convince you, to render yourself indefensible
But, when the wolves descend
They got that way, for a reason
There is no higher pedestal than to call a friend, family.

Frederik Sandfeld Hansen (Federicão Safadão)
"E Rudhi Dina, heshidhanii... ne Lisaan al-Gayib!"
Bio
about_details:
The world is like a ride in an amusement park, and when you choose to go on it you think it's real because that's how powerful our minds are. The ride goes up and down, around and around, it has thrills and chills, and it's very brightly colored, and it's very loud, and it's fun for a while. Many people have been on the ride a long time, and they begin to wonder, "Hey, is this real, or is this just a ride?" And other people have remembered, and they come back to us and say, "Hey, don't worry; don't be afraid, ever, because this is just a ride." And we … kill those people. "Shut him up! I've got a lot invested in this ride, shut him up! Look at my furrows of worry, look at my big bank account, and my family. This has to be real." It's just a ride. But we always kill the good guys who try and tell us that, you ever notice that? And let the demons run amok … But it doesn't matter, because it's just a ride. And we can change it any time we want. It's only a choice. No effort, no work, no job, no savings of money. Just a simple choice, right now, between fear and love. The eyes of fear want you to put bigger locks on your doors, buy guns, close yourself off. The eyes of love instead see all of us as one. Here's what we can do to change the world, right now, to a better ride. Take all that money we spend on weapons and defenses each year and instead spend it feeding and clothing and educating the poor of the world, which it would pay for many times over, not one human being excluded, and we could explore space, together, both inner and outer, forever, in peace.
"To make a truly miserable man, have him believe that he can not change his future, yet have him believe that he could have changed his past."

Trying to get healthy and physically fit for the rest of my life! Not an easy task y'all!
Learn to love by loving. (Iris Murloch)

intro: Personal details
about_details:
I refuse to categorize myself, though I'm sure that doesn't stop others... At any rate, I am still discovering things about myself and most likely will continue to do so for some time. One thing that I think it would be safe to mention about myself, as it has stuck with me from my first memories till now is; I like to draw and paint pictures. I also like writing both prose/poetry and music. As for the rest of who I am, I think my opinion of myself is still not completely reckoned, as I continue to grow. Though I do have what seem to be core values like, a soft spot for the underdog, and the respect of the varying beliefs of others (I find actions more defining of one's character), I don't feel the need to affiliate myself with large groups, politically, religiously, or socially. I will stand up for what I feel is right and strive to not be part of what I feel is wrong and if there happens to be, or not, a group that agrees/disagrees with my morals, so be it, I still wish not to exclude those who's values differ from mine as I feel we are better served learning from one another than fighting although I will admit, some battles will most likely always be inevitable...
Imagination is more important than Knowledge. -Albert Einstein
Just listen to your heart, that's what I do. -Napoleon Dynamite
The wealth of money must never supersede the richness of life. -Me

I have carried a baby in my body. I have comforted a baby on my chest. I have kissed booboos, been puked, peed & pooped on. Woke up to a hungry baby and stayed up all night with a sick baby. But I wouldn't have it any other way. My body isn't magazine perfect, but when I look in the mirror, I see a Mom, and there is no... greater honor or blessing.
"You can't fix stupid." –––Ron White

about_details:
Married since 27 November 1982
Joyfully married for 29 years. Have four wonderful children. Have worked as a Chemical Engineer for 30 years.
Wrote two books: the first was "THE PAPER TRAIL" and the second was "STILLBORN . Both are fictional books based loosely on parts of my life.
THE PAPER TRAIL is about growing up in Oaklyn, serving newspapers, and teen friendships. The story also details the history of the town of Smithville which is near Mt. Holly and close to where I live now. The book starts slow and peaceful, then picks up pace at the middle. The story line will surprise you and make you think. If you read it and finish it, ask yourself if the boys did the right thing or not.
STILLBORN is based on the summer of 1969 when men first lnded on the moon and I spent time with my grandparents. It takes place in Cape May Point and gives a wonderful history of Cape May. Read it to the end and you will be pleasantly surprized, especially if you have children.
Both books are available on Amazon. Type the title and then William Platt and they will show up.
